**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Right‑of‑way” rules for merging, turning, and highway exits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing on either side of a stopped bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other vehicles.
• Maintain safe following distance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Pay attention to posted signs for time limits. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Toll Roads & Bridges** | • Texas has several toll roads (e.g., Sam Houston Tollway, LBJ Freeway).
• Use electronic toll tags (e‑Tag) for convenience. | TxDOT Toll Operations | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Trucks over 10,000 lb must have a commercial driver’s license (CDL).
• Bicyclists must obey traffic signals and ride in the lane when possible. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Emergency Vehicle Exemptions** | • Police, fire, ambulance, and other emergency vehicles may use the right lane and ignore certain traffic signals when responding to emergencies. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – For road conditions, construction, and official speed limit changes. - **TxDMV** – For registration, licensing, and inspection requirements. - **Texas Legislature Online** – For the most recent statutes and amendments. - **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic violation penalties and court procedures. --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas 1. **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. 2. **Avoid distractions** – no texting, no handheld phone use. 3. **Observe posted speed limits** – they can change at construction zones or in school districts. 4. **Respect school buses** – they have the right of way when stopping to pick up or drop off children. 5. **Use your turn signals** – they’re required by law and help prevent accidents. If you need detailed legal language or specific case law, let me know and I can pull up the relevant statutes or recent court decisions!
